brief: Mattresses and bedding, 100-night trial, free shipping and returns. Mattresses run $600-2,000. It's a once-every-8-years purchase so we want people who just moved or are renovating.

profile.business_summary: The advertiser sells mattresses and bedding, offering a 100-night trial with free shipping and returns. Their mattresses range from $600 to $2,000. Because mattresses are an infrequent purchase (once every 8 years), they target consumers undergoing major life transitions such as moving or renovating.

pricing.rationale: Pay per click (verifiable without trusting a pixel). Market price to win a page view on these hosts: $0.83-$1.10 per click (median $0.95), from the simulated auction against the other campaigns. 'balanced' bidding tries to win up to 60% of each host's page views; the planned bid per host is the price that wins its planned share.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded.

allocations.rationale: market price $0.83-$1.10 (median $0.95); bidding $0.66 wins ~4% of page views, paying ~$0.62 per click (second price); host also sells this kind of product: confirm it allows competing brands
market price $0.83-$1.08 (median $0.92); bidding $0.64 wins ~1% of page views, paying ~$0.61 per click (second price)

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: planned bid per host; pacing only
phases.why: stable bids so measured rates aren't confounded

phases.name: maximize
phases.rule: planned bid x pacing x conversion likelihood, up to the ceiling

adjustments.reason: Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.
Bid higher when the shopper looks like a likely converter (persona match vs the host's average shopper).

bid_strategy.rationale: Maximise conversions within the budget; the ceiling per host is the price that wins your 'balanced' share.
